name: IonQ
description: IonQ builds quantum computers that use trapped ions as qubits and sells access to them mainly through the cloud (Amazon Braket, Microsoft Azure Quantum, Google Cloud Marketplace and its own cloud), plus contracts to build specialised quantum hardware for governments and research customers. In 2025 and 2026 it bought its way into a broader 'quantum platform': quantum networking and security (id Quantique), sensing (Vector Atomic), radar-satellite data (Capella Space), photonics (Lightsynq), a chip-control technology (Oxford Ionics) and, after 2026-06-30, a US semiconductor foundry (SkyWater, about $1.8B). Revenue is small ($130M in 2025) and heavily concentrated (three customers were 53% of 2025 revenue); operating losses ($634M in 2025) are far larger than sales, and reported profit swings by billions because of warrants marked to market.

businessLines.name: Single reportable segment (quantum computing, networking, sensing, space data)
businessLines.how: Cloud access fees for quantum computing time (revenue recognised on the cloud provider's billing without end-user mark-up), fixed-price contracts to build quantum hardware for governments and research centres (recognised over time as work progresses), plus product and data sales from acquired businesses.
businessLines.description: 10-K: one operating segment. Offerings: quantum computing as a service (QCaaS), quantum hardware built to order, professional services, quantum networking/security, sensing, and satellite radar data; product-line revenue split not extracted.
